Consult Summary:
- 2 months of work-triggered anxiety with insomnia and morning palpitations, low mood/anhedonia, no suicidal ideation; plan for NHS talking therapy, online resources, sleep advice, and basic blood tests with GP follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Escalating anxiety for ~2 months, primarily related to starting a new, highly stressful job; morning dread of leaving the house; palpitations.
- Timeline/progression: Began ~2 months ago, coinciding with new job; symptoms have been worsening.
- Daily impact:
  - Sleep: Bed 10–11 pm; prolonged sleep latency (“hours”); wakes before alarm with racing heart; shallow sleep; estimates 3–4 hours/night.
  - Daytime: Very low energy; anhedonia; on edge; impaired enjoyment of hobbies (running, tennis) and socializing; avoids some social contact.
  - Work: Dreads going; has not missed work but frequently considers calling in sick; difficult interactions with supervisor.
- Triggers/exacerbating factors: Work-related stress; mornings; fear of being late; public transport (especially warm, airless tube).
- Palpitations: Fast, perceived irregular beats, lasting a few minutes up to ~10 minutes; occur mainly in mornings with anticipatory stress; no typical chest pain (discomfort only when heart races).
- Associated symptoms: Low mood most days, constant worry; persistent anxiety even on weekends (less intense); appetite largely unchanged (more chocolate).
- Pertinent negatives: No history of similar episodes; denies panic attacks; denies suicidal thoughts or intent; no illicit drug use.

Past Medical History:
- Not recorded.

Medications:
- Current medications: Not recorded.
- Allergies: Not recorded.

Social History:
- Lives with parents; supportive family.
- Occupation: Head office role at a fashion retailer; new to sector; high stress; reports boss is unkind.
- Alcohol: Binge-level intake on Fridays/Saturdays (“over my limit”); occasional glass of wine during the week; does not closely track.
- Tobacco: Occasional smoking.
- Illicit drugs: Denied.
- Exercise/hobbies: Previously ran and played tennis; currently reduced due to low enjoyment.

Family History:
- Mother with past depression.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- Plan for basic blood tests to evaluate palpitations/possible triggers (specific tests not documented); GP follow-up planned one week after tests to review results.
- No prior test results discussed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Work-related anxiety with associated depressive symptoms and significant insomnia; palpitations likely anxiety-related. Medical contributors to palpitations to be screened with basic blood tests.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (work-related): Onset with new stressful job; prominent work-focused anxiety, low mood, anhedonia, functional impact. Opposes: Symptoms persist somewhat on weekends.
  - Generalized anxiety disorder (early course): Excessive worry, insomnia, fatigue, impairment. Opposes: Duration ~2 months and worries largely centered on work.
  - Hyperthyroidism (low likelihood): Anxiety/insomnia/palpitations can fit. Opposes: No classic hyperthyroid features reported; clear psychosocial trigger.

- Issue 1: Work-related anxiety with low mood (no suicidality)
  - Plan:
    - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (link to be provided).
    - Use recommended online self-help resources now (to be provided).
    - Safety net: Call back if symptoms worsen, if unable to cope with work/ADLs, or if no benefit from initial strategies.
    - No medication initiated today; may be considered if inadequate response to therapy or worsening symptoms (as discussed).

- Issue 2: Palpitations (likely anxiety-related)
  - Plan:
    - Arrange basic blood tests via support line (patient to call).
    - GP follow-up one week after tests to review and determine need for further evaluation.
    - Education: Likely anxiety-related; monitor frequency/duration.

- Issue 3: Insomnia related to anxiety
  - Plan:
    - Provide sleep hygiene guidance/resources (to be added to notes).
    - Address underlying anxiety as per Issue 1.

- General plan items:
  - Patient to contact support line to schedule blood tests.
  - Book GP follow-up ~1 week post-testing to review results and next steps.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Past medical history, current medication list, and allergies not documented; vitals and physical exam not recorded; specific blood tests not listed.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some utterances unclear/inaudible in places; no objective measurements available due to teleconsultation.
